title.narrative: Smart Water Management for Surface Water and Groundwater

description.narrative: With the increasing pressure on water resources and ongoing industrial and urban development, river basin organisations in Central Java increasingly embed conjunctive use of surface- and groundwater into their strategies for future water management. As they aim to meet future water demand, they try to make optimal and sustainable use of available surface and groundwater resources, a development locally recognised as ‘smart water management’.Combining the views on surface water and groundwater is non-conventional to the Indonesian context, as government mandate of surface water and groundwater lies with two different ministries, the Ministry of Public Works and Housing (PUPR) and Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, respectively. A joint development of a Smart Water Management System (SWMS) has been suggested by the Indonesian counterparts to catalyse this improved cooperation, improve the local understanding of the (condition) of the water system (ground and surface), improve data availability and accessibly and, eventually, lead to better policy- development and -implementation for water distribution, spatial development and land-use planning.The actual driver for development of a SWMS is the rapidly increasing (bulk) water demand for rural, industrial, and agricultural purposes and the uncontrolled and increasing extraction of groundwater, leading to alarming land subsidence and coastal erosion in almost the entire Northern Java region. Semarang and its surroundings, Central Java, is chosen as pilot area.A two-phased approach is applied:- Phase I: Reconnaissance and inception to verify and consolidate (local) stakeholder involvement, to create a common understanding amongst them and to jointly define the requirements for a SWMS. In case of positive outcomes of Phase I,- Phase II: SWMS development.This assignment concerns Phase I only.Eventually project success will be determined by:1) Successful joint development of an operational and functional SWMS;2) Effective use and integration of the SWMS in the local water management decision making;3) Improved local institutional coordination and cooperation leading to a more integrated ground- and surface water management, land-use planning and spatial development. Starting in Semarang and its surroundings with eventual implementation for the entire Northern Java region.
